texts: After thoracoabdominal aneurysm repair, five-year survival averages between 50 and 70 percent: six or seven of the ten chairs are taken at the reunion: D.
Survival is lowest after the most extensive repairs and in older patients with kidney failure or heart and lung disease.

Death in hospital, complications and spinal cord injury vary widely with the extent of the repair and the experience of the centre, and the figures offered in the other options are not those of the book.
Memory hook: five candles, ten chairs, and only six or seven sailors to drink.
